answer: Mint identities on a bonding curve: identity n costs c·n, fees burned. N sybils over H honest members then cost c(HN+N²/2) — quadratic, and the honest crowd raises the toll; copying keys is a zephyr, abundant air that buys no slot. Slots re-lock each epoch or decay like saffron losing aroma in open air, so cheap early stockpiles fade. The contract prices each mint; no owner must be identified. It deters only while per-identity lifetime reward stays below the curve price at depth, and latecomers pay an incumbent tax — calling that costless is a fable.
